 Hyderabad Top News Hyderabad Weather Today, October 23: Dry Conditions Likely Across Telangana, IMD Issues No Warnings
 Harsha Vardhini 23 Oct 2026 2:53 PM Share this: HYDERABAD: Hyderabad weather today, October 23, 2026, is expected to remain dry, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasting dry weather across Telangana for three consecutive days. The Meteorological Centre, Hyderabad, has issued no weather warnings for the state in its media weather bulletin dated October 23.
 The forecast also covers October 24 and 25. The latest bulletin does not specify Hyderabad’s temperature, humidity, wind speed or individual locality-wise conditions. Residents should not interpret the absence of warnings as a guarantee of identical weather across every neighbourhood. 
 Hyderabad weather today: Will it rain on October 23?
 The IMD has forecast dry weather across Telangana on Friday, October 23. The bulletin does not forecast rain or thunderstorms for Hyderabad in its stated outlook.

 The department has issued no weather warnings. It has not specified any yellow, orange or red alert for Hyderabad or other Telangana districts in this bulletin.
 The available report does not provide separate forecasts for Hyderabad’s individual zones, including Gachibowli, Secunderabad, Kukatpally, LB Nagar and Shamshabad. It also does not include observed temperatures, rainfall measurements, cloud cover or wind speeds. 
 Hyderabad weather tomorrow: Forecast for October 24
 Dry weather is likely to continue across Telangana on Saturday, October 24, according to the IMD. The same outlook applies to Sunday, October 25.
 The bulletin does not provide separate forecasts for Hyderabad, Ranga Reddy or Medchal-Malkajgiri districts. It also does not specify any district-level warning or expected rainfall amounts for these areas.
 Residents looking for a more detailed Hyderabad weather forecast should refer to updated official bulletins when available.
 Telangana weather forecast: What to expect over the next five days
 The October 23 media bulletin provides a three-day outlook, covering October 23–25. It does not provide enough information to establish a complete five-day forecast for October 23–27.
 Date IMD forecast 
 Friday, October 23 Dry weather likely across Telangana 
 Saturday, October 24 Dry weather likely across Telangana 
 Sunday, October 25 Dry weather likely across Telangana 
 Monday, October 26 Not specified in the supplied bulletin 
 Tuesday, October 27 Not specified in the supplied bulletin 
 The IMD has also reported a low-pressure area over the southeast and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal. The system is likely to intensify into a depression on October 24 and a deep depression on October 25. It is forecast to intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26.
 The system is expected to move towards the north Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts over the following two days. The bulletin does not forecast a direct impact on Telangana from this system.
 Telangana weather today: Are any districts under alert?
 The IMD’s October 23 media weather bulletin states that there are no weather warnings for Telangana. It does not identify any districts under yellow, orange or red alerts.
 The bulletin also says a low-pressure area over the southeast Arabian Sea, off south Kerala, has no further influence over Telangana.
 No district-wise thunderstorm warning, lightning alert, heavy rainfall warning or wind-speed forecast is included in the supplied bulletin.
 IMD weather advisory: What should residents do?
 With dry weather forecast and no warnings issued, the bulletin does not specify any weather-related emergency precautions for Hyderabad.
 Residents should continue to follow routine weather updates and check fresh IMD advisories if conditions change. Any new warning should be assessed according to its stated location, validity period and weather hazard.
 Why is Telangana expected to remain dry?
 The IMD’s latest outlook forecasts dry conditions across Telangana for October 23–25. It separately describes developing weather systems over the Bay of Bengal and the southeast Arabian Sea.
 The bulletin does not establish a direct link between the Bay of Bengal system and any expected weather change in Hyderabad during this period.
